stories.headline: Anthropic accuses Alibaba of largest-ever distillation attack, 28.8M Claude exchanges via 25K fake accounts

key_facts.fact: Anthropic accused Alibaba of waging the largest known distillation attack against its Claude models, telling US senators and White House officials that operators linked to Alibaba's Qwen AI lab used nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts to extract Claude's capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: telling senators and White House officials that operators linked to Alibaba's Qwen AI lab used nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts to extract Claude's capabilities between April and June

key_facts.fact: The campaign ran between April 22 and June 5, 2026, and generated more than 28.8 million exchanges with Claude through almost 25,000 fraudulent accounts.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said the campaign was conducted between April 22 and June 5, 2026, and generated more than 28.8 million exchanges with Claude through almost 25,000 fraudulent accounts.

key_facts.fact: The campaign targeted Claude's most commercially valuable skills, software engineering and agentic reasoning, and Anthropic said it was a way to accelerate China's ability to reach Anthropic's advanced Mythos Preview capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said in the letter that distillation is a way to help accelerate China's ability to reach Anthropic's advanced Mythos Preview capabilities.

key_facts.fact: The letter, dated June 10, was sent to Senators Tim Scott and Elizabeth Warren, chair and ranking member of the US Senate Banking Committee, ahead of a scheduled AI hearing.
key_facts.excerpt: The letter, dated June 10, was sent to Senators Tim Scott and Elizabeth Warren, the chair and ranking member, respectively, of the US Senate Banking Committee, ahead of a scheduled hearing on AI.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic warned that adversarial distillation lets Chinese labs replicate frontier AI at a fraction of the training cost, that such models often lack safety guardrails, and urged the Trump administration to clarify antitrust guidelines, maintain chip export controls, and penalize firms that use the technique.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic warned that adversarial distillation lets Chinese labs replicate frontier AI at a fraction of the training cost, and that models built this way often lack safety guardrails.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba fell about 5% in Hong Kong after the accusation, taking its year-to-date decline to 33%, while Xiaomi and Baidu fell more than 3%.
key_facts.excerpt: ANTHROPIC accused Chinese technology giant Alibaba of waging a large-scale effort to "illicitly" access its Claude artificial intelligence model using thousands of fraudulent accounts

stories.headline: Mirendil, founded by ex-Anthropic researchers, raises $200M seed at $1B valuation to build self-improving AI R&D

key_facts.fact: Mirendil, a San Francisco AI lab founded by former Anthropic researchers, raised $200 million in seed funding at a valuation of roughly $1 billion, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins, with Nvidia participating among other investors.
key_facts.excerpt: AI startup Mirendil raised $200 million in seed funding at a $1 billion valuation, one of the largest AI seed rounds to date... The round was co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins, with NVIDIA participating as an investor.

key_facts.fact: The company is training frontier models that are expert at AI research and engineering, designed to loop over research and engineering problems autonomously and make progress without human intervention.
key_facts.excerpt: Mirendil is building a system that can help anyone do AI work: they train frontier models that are expert at AI R&D and build the product around it. The system is meant to loop over research and engineering problems more autonomously, and make more and more progress without human intervention.

key_facts.fact: The founding team consists of 20 researchers and engineers from frontier labs including Anthropic, xAI, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI; co-founders are Behnam Neyshabur, Harsh Mehta, Shayan Salehian, and Tara Rezaei.
key_facts.excerpt: Our founding team consists of 20 researchers and engineers from frontier institutions including Anthropic, xAI, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI

key_facts.fact: Mirendil's goal is to democratize frontier AI R&D so that labs working in drug discovery, chemistry, biology, or robotics no longer need to also become a frontier AI lab; the company aims to build a system 'that builds systems' and continually improves itself.
key_facts.excerpt: The lab that automates this loop will go beyond building better models. It will build the thing that is capable of continually improving itself toward any goal.

sources.title: Mirendil raises $200M in one of AI's biggest seed rounds

stories.headline: Google makes computer use a built-in tool in Gemini 3.5 Flash for browser, mobile and desktop agents

key_facts.fact: Google announced that computer use is now a built-in tool supported in Gemini 3.5 Flash, integrated natively into the main Flash model rather than only available as a standalone Gemini 2.5 computer use model.
key_facts.excerpt: Computer use is now a built-in tool supported in Gemini 3.5 Flash, delivering our best performance yet for agentic computer use tasks. Previously only available as a standalone Gemini 2.5 computer use model, computer use is now integrated natively in the main Gemini Flash model.

key_facts.fact: Developers can build custom agents that see, reason and take action across browser, mobile and desktop environments, improving performance for long-horizon and enterprise automation tasks like continuous software testing and knowledge work.
key_facts.excerpt: developers can now use 3.5 Flash to reliably build custom agents that can see, reason and take action across browser, mobile and desktop environments. This unlocks improved performance for long-horizon and enterprise automation tasks like continuous software testing and knowledge work across professional applications.

key_facts.fact: The capability is available via the Gemini API and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and introduces an 'intent' field explaining the model's reasoning behind each step, configurable safety policies, and opt-in prompt injection detection via screenshot scanning.
key_facts.excerpt: Streamlined actions with intents: actions include an `intent` field that explains the model's reasoning behind each step... Prompt injection detection: opt-in screenshot scanning to detect hidden adversarial instructions.

sources.title: Introducing computer use in Gemini 3.5 Flash

stories.headline: Google set to lose two more key Gemini researchers, Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel, to Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel, both viewed internally as key contributors to Google's Gemini model, are planning to leave for Anthropic; Adler worked on Google's AI coding effort and Pritzel was involved in training AI systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini contributors Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel planning to join rival AI developer Anthropic... Adler worked on Google's AI coding efforts, while Pritzel was involved in the process used to train AI systems.

key_facts.fact: Both researchers previously contributed to Google DeepMind's scientific work, listed among authors of the company's research expanding AlphaFold protein-structure predictions across entire proteomes, alongside Nobel laureate John Jumper, who is himself joining Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: They are listed among the authors of the company's work on expanding AlphaFold protein-structure predictions across entire proteomes, alongside AlphaFold researchers including John Jumper.

key_facts.fact: The departures add to a string of high-profile Google exits, including Nobel winner John Jumper heading to Anthropic and Transformer co-author Noam Shazeer leaving for OpenAI, alongside Sissie Hsiao and researcher Arthur Conmy.
key_facts.excerpt: Their departures add to a growing list of high-profile losses for Google... Noam Shazeer: Gemini co-lead and co-author of the landmark 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper, left Google to join OpenAI... John Jumper: Google DeepMind Vice President and a 2024 Nobel Prize winner... is leaving for Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: A 2025 SignalFire analysis found DeepMind engineers were nearly 11 times more likely to leave for Anthropic than the reverse; Jumper would likely not begin work at Anthropic until next year due to UK non-compete agreements.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepMind engineers are nearly 11 times more likely to leave for Anthropic than the reverse, according to a 2025 industry analysis from the venture capital firm SignalFire.

sources.title: Google reportedly set to lose two key Gemini and DeepMind researchers to Anthropic

stories.headline: Meta accelerates shift to LLMs for content and ad review, targeting 90% of human reviews replaced by year-end

key_facts.fact: Meta has already shifted roughly half of its content review requests to large language models this year and is planning to expand the use of AI further in the coming months.
key_facts.excerpt: The Financial Times reported that Meta has already shifted roughly half of its content review requests to large language models this year. The company is reportedly planning to expand the use of AI even further in the coming months.

key_facts.fact: Sources said human involvement could fall by more than 90% for certain categories of content before the end of the year, allowing AI systems to handle a much larger share of routine moderation decisions without human intervention.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources familiar with the matter said human involvement could fall by more than 90% for certain categories of content before the end of the year.

key_facts.fact: The shift is part of a broader cost-cutting effort as CEO Mark Zuckerberg pours billions into AI infrastructure, talent recruitment, and 'personal superintelligence', and could save Meta billions of dollars annually.
key_facts.excerpt: The shift is part of a broader effort to cut costs as CEO Mark Zuckerberg pours billions of dollars into AI infrastructure, talent recruitment, and the development of what he describes as 'personal superintelligence.'

sources.title: Meta AI content moderation plan could replace most human reviewers and save billions

stories.headline: Trase raises $107M seed led by Arch to build an AI agent operating system for healthcare and defense

key_facts.fact: Trase, an AI operating system company building an infrastructure layer for AI agents in industries like healthcare and defense, raised $107 million in seed funding led by Arch Venture Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: Trase, an AI operating system company, has raised $107 million in seed funding led by Arch Venture Partners, CEO Grant Verstandig tells Axios Pro exclusively.

key_facts.fact: The company, led by CEO Grant Verstandig, plans to be in the market for more than $125 million in Series A funding later this year.
key_facts.excerpt: The company will be in market for more than $125 million in Series A funding later this year.

key_facts.fact: Trase delivers governed AI for healthcare, government and enterprise, offering hundreds of agents ready to deploy in weeks; the McLean/Northern Virginia company emerged from stealth in November 2025 with a $10.5 million pre-seed and early partners including Duke Health and the Navy.
key_facts.excerpt: Agentic AI startup Trase emerges from stealth with a $10.5 million pre-seed... The Northern Virginia company helps healthcare and defense automate work, with early partners including Duke Health and the Navy.

stories.headline: Assort Health hits $1.2B valuation with $120M Series C led by Menlo Ventures for healthcare voice AI agents

key_facts.fact: Assort Health raised a $120 million Series C led by Menlo Ventures, reaching unicorn status at a $1.2 billion valuation; the round also drew Lightspeed Venture Partners, Felicis, First Round Capital, Chemistry, Joe Montana, Tau Ventures and Quiet Capital.
key_facts.excerpt: Assort Health picked up $120 million in series C funding, hitting unicorn status... Menlo Ventures led the round, and the series C also was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Felicis, First Round Capital, Chemistry, Joe Montana, Tau Ventures and Quiet Capital.

key_facts.fact: The San Francisco startup, launched in November 2023, has now raised over $222 million to date; it builds specialty-specific AI voice agents that automate scheduling, intake, referrals, document processing, medication refills, lab requests and payments.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, which launched in November 2023, has raised $222 million to date and hit a valuation of $1.2 billion with the series C funding.

key_facts.fact: Assort's proprietary model, Synapse, is trained on more than 190 million patient voice interactions, 62,000 care protocols and 1.6 million decision pathways, and integrates natively with EHR systems including Epic and Athena.
key_facts.excerpt: The platform is powered by more than 190 million patient interactions, 62,000 care protocols, and 1.6 million decision pathways, which the company says constitutes the largest proprietary specialty dataset in healthcare. It integrates natively with leading EHR systems including Epic and Athena.

sources.title: Assort Health scores $120M series C to scale voice AI agent platform for healthcare
